'''Valentin Amrhein''' (born 1 April 1971 in [[Lübeck]]) is a German-Swiss professor of [[zoology]] at the [[University of Basel]] and [[science journalist]].<ref name=":111">{{cite web|title=Website of University of Basel: Prof. Dr. Valentin Amrhein |url=https://camargue.unibas.ch/en/team/valentin-amrhein |access-date=2021-03-15}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{citation|periodical=TagesWoche|title=Der mit den Nachtigallen tanzt|language=German|url=https://tageswoche.ch/form/portraet/der-mit-den-nachtigallen-tanzt/|access-date=2021-03-15
|last=Alexandra von Ascheraden|year=2015}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> Together with [[Sander Greenland]] and others, he is a critic of [[statistical significance|significance thresholds]] in science<ref name=":10">{{cite journal|title=Scientists rise up against statistical significance|journal=Nature |last1=Amrhein|first1=Valentin|last2=Greenland|first2=Sander|last3=McShane|first3=Blake|date=2019|doi=10.1038/d41586-019-00857-9|volume=567|issue=7748 |pages=305–307|pmid=30894741|bibcode=2019Natur.567..305A |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Remove, rather than redefine statistical significance|journal=Nature Human Behaviour|volume=2|issue=1|page=4|url= http://rdcu.be/wbtc |year=2018 |last1=Amrhein|first1=Valentin|last2=Greenland|first2=Sander|doi=10.1038/s41562-017-0224-0|pmid=30980046|s2cid=256708339 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and he draws attention to [[misunderstandings of p-values]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=The earth is flat (p > 0.05): significance thresholds and the crisis of unreplicable research|journal=PeerJ|volume=5 |year=2017|article-number=e3544 |last1=Amrhein|first1=Valentin|last2=Korner-Nievergelt|first2=Fränzi|last3=Roth|first3=Tobias |doi=10.7717/peerj.3544|pmid=28698825 |pmc=5502092 |doi-access=free }}</ref> He is author of a comment in the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' on [[statistical significance]]<ref name=":10" /> that had the highest online attention score of all research outputs ever screened by [[Altmetric]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Research of the Month: It's time to retire statistical significance |url=https://www.altmetric.com/blog/research-of-the-month-its-time-to-retire-statistical-significance/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220518070404/https://www.altmetric.com/blog/research-of-the-month-its-time-to-retire-statistical-significance/ |access-date=2023-03-22|archive-date=2022-05-18 }}</ref>

== Life ==
Amrhein spent his school years in [[Bonn]]<ref name=":1">{{citation|periodical=Bz Basel|title=Das Paradies für schrille Vögel|language=German|url=https://www.bzbasel.ch/basel/basel-stadt/das-paradies-fuer-schrille-voegel-130224147|access-date=2021-03-15 |last=Andreas Fahrländer|year=2016}}</ref> and studied [[biology]] at the University of Basel between 1992 and 1999.<ref name=":3">{{cite web|title=Singing activity and spatial behaviour as sexually selected traits in the nightingale (Doctoral thesis with Curriculum vitae) |url=https://edoc.unibas.ch/91/1/DissB_6778.pdf |access-date=2021-03-15 |last=Amrhein|first=Valentin|date=2004}}</ref>  He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] on the [[nightingale]] in 2004,<ref name=":1" /> followed by a [[research fellow|research stay]] at the [[University of Oslo]]. Since 2004 he has been head of the [[research station]] [[Petite Camargue Alsacienne]]. Since 2006, Amrhein has taught [[ornithology]], [[conservation biology]] and [[statistics]] at the Zoological Institute of the University of Basel. In addition, he works as a science journalist, and from 2012 to 2016 he was head of communications at the [[Swiss Academies of Arts and Sciences]]. Since 2017 he has been [[editor]] of the [[scientific journal|journal]] ''Ornithologischer Beobachter''<ref>{{cite web|title=Ornithologischer Beobachter |url=https://ala-schweiz.ch/index.php/ornithologischer-beobachter/ueber-die-zeitschrift |access-date=2021-03-15}}</ref> at the [[Sempach Bird Observatory|Swiss Ornithological Institute Sempach]].<ref name=":111" />

Amrhein is married and father of three daughters.<ref name=":2" /> During his studies he played [[violin]] in various [[orchestras]] and [[chamber music]] formations.<ref name=":3" />

== Key publications ==
* Amrhein, V.; [[Sander Greenland|Greenland, S.]] & McShane, B. (2019). [https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-00857-9/ "Retire statistical significance" (print title), "Scientists rise up against statistical significance" (online title)]. ''Nature''.
* Amrhein, V.; Trafimow, D. & [[Sander Greenland|Greenland, S.]] (2019). [https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00031305.2018.1543137/ "Inferential statistics as descriptive statistics: there is no replication crisis if we don't expect replication"]. ''The American Statistician''.
* Amrhein, V. & [[Sander Greenland|Greenland, S.]] (2018). [https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-017-0224-0 "Remove, rather than redefine, statistical significance"]. ''Nature Human Behaviour''.
* Amrhein, V.; Korner-Nievergelt, F. & Roth, T. (2017). [https://peerj.com/articles/3544/ "The earth is flat (p > 0.05): significance thresholds and the crisis of unreplicable research"]. ''PeerJ''.
* Roth, T.; Plattner, M. & Amrhein, V. (2014). [https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0082490 "Plants, birds and butterflies: short-term responses of species communities to climate warming vary by taxon and with altitude"]. ''PLOS ONE''.
* Amrhein, V.; Korner, P. & Naguib, M. (2002). [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0003347202919743/ "Nocturnal and diurnal singing activity in the nightingale: correlations with mating status and breeding cycle"]. ''Animal Behaviour''.
